answer: Each identity registers a marble block, locks a 70-credit bond and cuts it at dawn. It mixes a single-use saffron tracer into the cut face, filing slab/tailings weights. An auditor checks slab plus tailings against the block weight and the saffron signature against that block. Doses are scarce each dawn: the k-th costs 20+3(k-1) credits, so the 1,000th costs 3,017; 1,000 fakes pay 1,518,500 plus 70,000 in bonds. A tracer-rental ring fails: a rented slab lacks its tailings and reuses a signature, so both bonds burn. An honest cutter pays 20 once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
